result.summary: Full S1-S14 pass over REQ-020 (registration for an open event, atomic capacity, qr_token issuance), branch feature/WF02-REQ-020, commit 11c8871. Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md in full, then git diff master...HEAD myself (18 files: apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (new), apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/{registration.ts (new), start.ts}, i18n additions, index.ts, tests). Read REVIEWER's step-02b for context only -- re-derived every claim myself rather than trusting it, per S4/S7/S8's status as this gate's named focus. S4 (TOKENS, PRIMARY FOCUS) -- PASS. generateQrToken (domain/registration.ts:82-84) is exactly `randomBytes(32).toString("hex")` from node:crypto -- 256 bits, well over the 128-bit floor, hex-encoded to a 64-char string, one call, no loop, no parameters, no I/O. Ran `git grep -n "Math.random" apps/bot/src` myself: zero matches anywhere in the tree (not just the token path) -- confirms no fallback/legacy predictable-token path exists anywhere in the codebase, not only in this diff. Confirmed generateQrToken is the ONLY call site that produces a qr_token (single grep for `qrToken =` / `generateQrToken(` across the diff -- one producer, in registerForEvent's step 8c, only for the admitted branch). DB-level backstop verified by reading db/schema.ts directly: `uniqueIndex("registrations_qr_token_unique").on(table.qrToken)` (line 287) already exists (REQ-011, unchanged) -- an astronomically unlikely collision would surface as a unique-constraint insert failure inside registerForEvent's transaction (an unhandled throw, rolling the whole transaction back), never a silent overwrite of another registration's token. This is the correct failure mode: loud and non-silent, even though no retry-on-collision logic exists (named explicitly as an accepted open question in REQ-020.md §9.3, not silently omitted). S7 (ATOMIC CAPACITY, PRIMARY FOCUS) -- PASS. Read registerForEvent (registration.ts:109-216) line by line: exactly one db.transaction; the events row is locked via `.for("update")` (line 129) for the full span; the existing-registration check (137-141) and admitted-count query (145-149) both run against `tx`, before the pure decideRegistrationOutcome call; the INSERT into registrations (178-187) and the audit-log write (201-208) are both inside the same transaction as the lock. Did not re-run REVIEWER's full 50-iteration/5-way/raw-lock concurrency proof (already independently reproduced and is not my job to repeat) -- ran the committed AC1 test myself once: `npx vitest run apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts --no-file-parallelism` -> 13/13 passed including the 20-iteration real-Postgres AC1 race (registration.db.test.ts:140-186), confirmed genuinely exercised against real Postgres (dbAvailable=true, tests reported passed not skipped). NEW SCRUTINY (my own, not repeated from REVIEWER): searched for any other write path into the registrations table that could bypass the lock. `git grep -n "insert(registrations)" apps/bot/src` returns exactly one match: registration.ts:179, inside registerForEvent's own locked transaction. No other domain or handler file inserts into `registrations` anywhere in the codebase (checked domain/event.ts, domain/eventStaff.ts, domain/venue.ts, all handlers) -- registerForEvent is structurally the only path that can create a registrations row, so no stray direct insert exists that could bypass the lock and cause an over-admission. S8 (AUDIT LOG, PRIMARY FOCUS -- explicit S8-reading question). Confirmed by reading registration.ts:201-208: writeAuditLog is called exactly once per writing outcome, inside the same transaction as the INSERT, with action `registration.admit` for admitted and `registration.waitlist` for waitlisted -- both branches write, neither writes twice, no refusal outcome writes at all (step 7 returns before reaching step 8's writeAuditLog call for every non-writing kind). Verified against registration.db.test.ts's AC7 block (lines 320-378): explicit assertions for exactly-one-row on admitted, exactly-one-row on waitlisted, AND exactly-zero-rows on a refusal outcome -- all three cases tested, not just the admitted happy path. Ran this test suite myself, all passed. My own resolution of the S8/AC7 reading question (REQ-020.md §9.4): I AGREE with the design gate's resolution (audit both admitted and waitlisted). Reasoning, independent of the design doc's own argument: S8's own negative case is explicit -- "a status changed through a bulk/admin path that bypasses the audit-writing code path used by the normal path" -- and a `registrations` row moving from nonexistent to `waitlisted` is a real status change with real consequences (it creates a durable record an organizer later acts on, e.g. promoting from the waitlist), not a no-op. From a security standpoint specifically: an unaudited waitlist admission would leave no trace of who joined a waitlist, when, or via what source -- exactly the kind of accountability gap S8 exists to close, and there is no security argument for treating waitlisted as less audit-worthy than admitted (if anything, waitlist promotion is a later privileged action that will itself need to reference this originating row). AC7's narrower literal text does not carve out an exception; it simply doesn't test the broader case. Treating S8 (the security invariant) as governing over AC7's narrower literal wording is the correct precedence here, and this design applies it correctly with no unaudited status-change path introduced. S1 -- PASS, N/A beyond the existing gate. No new personal data is stored: a registrations row carries user_id (already-consented FK), admission, source (free-text channel label, not PII), qr_token (opaque). Reaching the Register button at all already required consent_pd_at non-null via the existing REQ-016 deep-link gate (unchanged) -- confirmed by reading resolveEventDeepLink (handlers/start.ts) still gates the write-capable branch on hasConsented before this diff's button is ever rendered. Registration itself adds no new consent-relevant write. S2 -- N/A, reason: registration has no role/EventStaff authorization surface -- every role may register (design §7.1 step 2 explicit, matches PRD: registering for an event is not a privileged action). resolveActingUser is used only to resolve identity, not to gate by role. S3 -- PASS. Confirmed the confirmation/refusal messages (handlers/registration.ts composeRegistrationReply, lines 104-139) surface only: catalog copy, the event's own title/date-time (public event metadata, not personal data), and (for already-registered) the CALLING user's own admission status read from THEIR OWN outcome object -- never another user's data. registerForEvent's every DB read is scoped by (eventId, userId) where userId is always the resolved acting user's own id (handlers/registration.ts:48, from resolveActingUser(db, tgId) against the caller's own Telegram id) -- no cross-user read path exists in this diff. source/pending_source attribution race -- checked as directed. getPendingSource/clearPendingSource (registration.ts:174, 197-199) both key exclusively on `userId` (the resolving user's own id, never taken from another user's context) and both run inside registerForEvent's own single transaction -- the read (step 8a) and the conditional clear (step 8e) happen in the same transaction as each other and as the insert, so no other transaction can observe or mutate this user's pending_source between the read and the clear (it's protected by the same events-row lock's serialization for concurrent registrations on the SAME event/user pair, and for a different event the two transactions don't share pending_source access patterns that could interleave incorrectly since it's a per-user column read-then-cleared-then-committed atomically). Confirmed via registration.db.test.ts's AC5 block: source='linkedin' correctly attributed and pending_source verified NULL afterward, and a second unrelated registration without a fresh pending_source correctly falls back to 'direct' rather than inheriting a stale value. No cross-user misattribution path found. S5/S6 -- N/A, no check-in or checked_in_at code touched by this diff. S9/S10 -- N/A, no notification/broadcast/scheduler code touched. S11 -- PASS. Grepped handlers/registration.ts and domain/registration.ts for any log/console call: zero matches. No phone/email is ever read, stored, or referenced by this diff's code (registrations carries no PII columns beyond the FK) -- S11 is satisfied vacuously and correctly, confirmed by grep not by the design's own claim. S12 -- N/A, no CSV export code touched. S13 -- N/A, no migration in this diff. Confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat`: no new file under apps/bot/drizzle/, matching REQ-020.md §10's explicit "no schema change" claim, verified independently by reading db/schema.ts myself and confirming every column this design touches (registrations.qr_token/source/admission, events.requires_invite/requires_approval/registration_closes_at/capacity) already existed pre-diff. No sign-off needed since no DDL is introduced. S14 -- N/A, publish_consent/speaker publication surface untouched. requires_invite/requires_approval refusal ordering (checked as directed) -- CONFIRMED SAFE. decideRegistrationOutcome (registration.ts:48-74) is a pure function with no I/O called from registerForEvent's step 6, BEFORE step 7's branch on outcome.kind; step 7 returns immediately, unwritten, for any outcome other than admitted/waitlisted -- requires-invite and requires-approval are both returned at rows 5-6 of the table, strictly before row 7 (capacity) and strictly before step 8 (the only step that ever calls INSERT). There is no code path by which a requires_invite=true or requires_approval=true event can reach the INSERT statement -- a misconfigured or malicious event flag can only ever produce a refusal outcome, never an admission, confirmed by reading the control flow directly (not by trusting the design's claim) and by registration.db.test.ts's AC6 block (lines 294-317) asserting `outcome` equals exactly `{ kind: "requires-invite" }` / `{ kind: "requires-approval" }` with capacity=5 (seats available) -- proving the gate fires even when capacity would otherwise admit. Commands run myself, real output: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, outside apps/bot). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (apps/web next build, apps/bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite) -> 15 files / 172 passed, 0 failures. `npx vitest run apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts --no-file-parallelism` (targeted re-run) -> 13/13 passed against real Postgres, including AC1's 20-iteration concurrency race, AC6's requires_invite/requires_approval-before-capacity refusal, and AC7's three-way audit-row assertion (admitted/waitlisted/zero-on-refusal). No S1-S14 violation found. All applicable items PASS; N/A items stated with reasons above, none silently skipped.
